must_remember: Stokes' theorem relates a surface integral of the curl of a vector field over an open surface $S$ to the line integral of the vector field around its boundary curve $C$: $\oint_C \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r} = \iint_S (\nabla \times \mathbf{F}) \cdot \mathbf{n} \, dS$.
The orientation of the boundary curve $C$ and the surface unit normal vector $\mathbf{n}$ must be consistent according to the right-hand rule.
A vector field is irrotational if and only if its curl vanishes everywhere: $\nabla \times \mathbf{F} = 0$.
Conservative forces (such as electrostatic and gravitational forces) possess zero curl, making work done around any closed loop zero and the line integral path-independent.
The value of the surface integral depends solely on the boundary curve $C$ and is invariant under the choice of the spanning open surface $S$.

glossary.heading: Statement of Stokes' Theorem
glossary.meaning: A fundamental theorem in vector calculus converting a surface integral of a curl over an open surface into a line integral around its boundary.

glossary.heading: Physical Interpretation of Curl
glossary.meaning: A differential operator representing the infinitesimal circulation or local rotation rate of a vector field at a point, denoted as $\nabla \times \mathbf{F}$.

glossary.heading: Relation to Conservative Forces
glossary.meaning: A vector field whose curl is identically zero throughout its domain, equivalent to being conservative.

glossary.heading: Orientation and Boundary Rules
glossary.meaning: A convention relating the positive direction of traversal along a boundary curve $C$ to the direction of the surface normal $\mathbf{n}$.
